prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2010 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core vision
- Replace “big government” with a “Big Society”: devolve power from central government to individuals, families, professionals and communities; promote responsibility, enterprise and transparency; insist “we’re all in this together.”

Economy and public finances
- Urgent deficit reduction: emergency budget; Office for Budget Responsibility; protect NHS/aid while cutting waste (£6bn in 2010/11), freezing most public pay for a year (excluding lowest paid), curbing quangos, ministers’ pay cuts, smaller Commons.
- Cancel most of Labour’s 2011 National Insurance rise for workers under £35k and employers; fund via waste cuts.
- Pro-business tax and regulation: cut corporation tax to 25% (small firms to 20%) funded by relief simplification; five-year corporate tax roadmap; Office of Tax Simplification; regulatory budgets; faster start-up registration; open procurement to SMEs.
- Balanced growth: boost exports, hi‑tech and green sectors; implement Dyson review; improve R&D credits; reform planning (abolish IPC; presumption for sustainable development).
- Skills and jobs: single Work Programme with payment by results; reassess incapacity benefits; “work for the dole” for long-term claimants; NIC holiday for first 10 hires in new firms; 400,000 apprenticeships/training places; new all-age careers service.
- Banking reform: bank levy; end tripartite regime—BoE to supervise prudential risk; curb risky trading; promote competition; “people’s bank bonus.”
- Infrastructure and regions: begin national high-speed rail; oppose new runways at Heathrow/Stansted/Gatwick; reform rail franchises; superfast broadband via existing infrastructure; local enterprise partnerships; incentives for private-sector growth outside SE.
- Immigration: annual non‑EU cap; tighter student visas; integration/English tests.

Society: families, schools, welfare, crime, NHS
- Families: recognise marriage/civil partnerships in tax; end tax credit couple penalty; two‑year council tax freeze; expand flexible working; relationship support; curb commercialisation of childhood; refocus Sure Start on early intervention; 4,200 more health visitors.
- Education: tougher discipline; elevate teaching standards (Teach First/Now, Troops to Teachers); rigorous curriculum, phonics and age‑6 reading test; reform exams; pupil premium; expand academies/free schools; protect special schools; technical academies.
- Welfare: make work pay; sanctions for refusal of reasonable jobs; SME support and entrepreneurship loans.
- Crime/justice: elected police commissioners; cut paperwork; tougher knife sentences; overhaul alcohol licensing (ban below‑cost sales, higher fines); honesty in sentencing; rehabilitation via payment by results; border police force.
- NHS and care: real-terms funding rises; patient choice across qualified providers; GP‑led commissioning; scrap non‑clinical targets; transparency of outcomes; 24/7 urgent care access; Cancer Drugs Fund; integrated health/social-care budgets; support carers; voluntary insurance option for residential care; shift to public health with outcomes-based funding.

Politics and civil liberties
- Clean up Westminster: MP recall; donation cap agreement; lobby rules; cut costs; equalise constituencies; more public participation (e‑petitions, Public Reading Stage); publish spending/salaries/contracts; cut quangos; strong localism (neighbourhood planning, referendums, community right to buy/bid).
- Civil liberties: scrap ID cards/National Identity Register/ContactPoint; UK Bill of Rights; limit DNA retention; scale back vetting.

Environment and energy
- 80% emissions cut by 2050; 10% Whitehall reduction in year one.
- Green economy: Green Investment Bank; carbon floor price; environmental tax shift; smart grid/meters; CCS on four plants; support nuclear (no subsidy), offshore wind/marine; “Green Deal” home upgrades; protect habitats, fisheries reform, animal welfare; tree planting; sustainable farming (no GM unless proven safe); clearer food labelling; waste “Responsibility Deal.”

National interest, defence, aid and EU
- National Security Council; Strategic Defence and Security Review; renew Trident; defence procurement reform; restore Military Covenant (higher operational allowance, military wards, scholarships for bereaved children).
- Foreign policy: liberal Conservative—human rights, alliances (US, India, others), Afghan mission, prevent Iranian nukes, two‑state solution.
- EU: positive but guarded; referendum lock on future power transfers; no Euro; Sovereignty Bill; seek repatriation of powers over social/employment, justice and rights.
- Aid: meet 0.7% of GNI by 2013 in law; transparency, results focus; stop aid to China/Russia; focus on basics and Commonwealth; £500m/year to fight malaria; promote trade-led development and stabilization capacity.
